strings.name: Narges Mohammadi
strings.role: Iranian human rights activist · Nobel Peace laureate
strings.summary: Trained in physics, Mohammadi campaigns for Iranian women’s rights, political prisoners and abolition of the death penalty, enduring repeated detention. She received the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize in prison. Arrested again in 2025, she received another 7½-year sentence in February 2026, supporters said. Her foundation reported medical suspension and hospital transfer in May; she gave an AP interview in September. Medical release is neither acquittal nor permanent freedom, and health details remain limited.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Long advocating women’s rights in Iran and opposing the death penalty, she received the Nobel Peace Prize for this work; her detention has attracted international attention.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Women’s rights and Nobel prize
strings.highlights.h1.text: Received the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for fighting women’s oppression in Iran and promoting human rights and freedom for all.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied physics at Imam Khomeini University in Qazvin.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Advocacy amid detention
strings.highlights.h2.text: Continued women’s-rights and abolition campaigns despite repeated sentences and imprisonment; health and medical care drew concern.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Interview
strings.timeline.t1.text: Gave an interview to the Associated Press.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Medical sentence suspension
strings.timeline.t2.text: Her foundation reported suspension on heavy bail and transfer to Tehran for treatment.
strings.timeline.t3.title: New 7½-year sentence
strings.timeline.t3.text: Her foundation and lawyer reported a sentence on assembly, collusion and propaganda-related charges.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Arrest at memorial
strings.timeline.t4.text: Arrested after speaking at lawyer Khosrow Alikordi’s memorial; authorities accused her of disturbing order.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: Still imprisoned, with her children accepting the award.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Sixteen-year sentence
strings.timeline.t6.text: Sentenced over activities including death-penalty opposition; later released and arrested again.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins rights organization
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joined the Defenders of Human Rights Centre, assisting political prisoners and opposing executions.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Zanjan
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Iran, later studied physics and entered public activism.
